sentences.zh: 高祖初即位，將改周制，乃下詔曰：「宣尼制法，云行夏之時，乘殷之輅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu first ascended the throne, intending to reform Zhou regulations, he issued an edict saying: "Confucius established the law, saying 'Follow the Xia calendar, ride in the Yin carriage.'
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu first took the throne, intending to reform Northern Zhou institutions, he issued an edict: "Confucius established the law, saying, 'Follow the Xia calendar; ride in the Yin carriage.'

sentences.zh: 弈葉共遵，理無可革。

translations.literal: Generation after generation all followed it; by principle there was nothing to change.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation all followed this; in principle nothing could be changed.

sentences.zh: 然三代所尚，眾論多端，或以為所建之時，或以為所感之瑞，或當其行色，因以從之。

translations.literal: Yet what the Three Dynasties honored gave rise to many divergent views—some held it was the season of their dynastic founding, some the auspicious omen they responded to, or it matched the color of their prevailing element, and thus they followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the Three Dynasties honored gave rise to many divergent views—some held it was the season of their dynastic founding, some the auspicious omen they responded to, or it matched the color of their prevailing element, and thus they followed it.

sentences.zh: 今雖夏數得天，歷代通用，漢尚於赤，魏尚於黃，驪馬玄牲，已弗相踵，明不可改，建寅歲首，常服於黑。

translations.literal: Though the Xia calendar reckoned heaven correctly and has been used universally through the dynasties, Han honored red, Wei honored yellow, bay horses and dark sacrificial victims no longer followed in succession—clearly they could not be changed; establishing yin as the year-start, ordinary dress honored black.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Xia calendar reckoned heaven correctly and has been used universally through the dynasties, Han honored red and Wei honored yellow; bay horses and dark sacrificial victims no longer followed in succession—clearly they could not be changed. With yin established as the year-start, ordinary dress honored black.

sentences.zh: 朕初受天命，赤雀來儀，兼姬周已還，於茲六代。

translations.literal: When I first received Heaven's mandate, the red bird came in auspicious omen; counting from the Ji clan of Zhou down to now, there have been six dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: When I first received Heaven's mandate, the red bird came as an auspicious omen; counting from the house of Ji-Zhou to the present, there have now been six dynasties.

sentences.zh: 三正廻復，五德相生，總以言之，並宜火色。

translations.literal: The three calendars circulate and return, the Five Virtues generate one another—taking all together, all should favor the color of fire.
translations.idiomatic: The three calendars circulate and return, and the Five Virtues generate one another—taking all together, all should favor the color of fire.

sentences.zh: 垂衣已降，損益可知，尚色雖殊，常兼前代。

translations.literal: From the era of 'draping robes' down to the present, additions and subtractions can be known; though the honored color differs, it commonly includes the previous dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: From the era of 'draping robes' down to the present, additions and subtractions can be known; though the honored color differs, it commonly incorporates the previous dynasty.

sentences.zh: 其郊丘廟社，可依袞冕之儀，朝會衣裳，宜盡用赤。

translations.literal: For suburban altars, ancestral temples, and earth-god shrines, one may follow the guanmian ritual; for court assemblies and ceremonial dress, one should use red entirely.
translations.idiomatic: For suburban altars, ancestral temples, and earth-god shrines, one may follow the guanmian ritual; for court assemblies and ceremonial dress, red should be used throughout.

sentences.zh: 昔丹烏木運，姬有大白之旂，黃星土德，曹乘黑首之馬，在祀與戎，其尚恒異。

translations.literal: In antiquity the red bird governed the Wood cycle, the Ji clan had great white banners; the yellow star marked the Earth Virtue, Cao [Wei] rode horses with black heads—in sacrifice and warfare, what they honored always differed.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the red bird governed the Wood cycle, and the house of Ji had great white banners; the yellow star marked the Earth Virtue, and Cao Wei rode horses with black heads—in sacrifice and warfare, what they honored always differed.

sentences.zh: 今之戎服，皆可尚黃，在外常所著者，通用雜色。

translations.literal: Present military dress may all honor yellow; what is ordinarily worn outside may generally use mixed colors.
translations.idiomatic: Present military dress may all honor yellow; what is ordinarily worn outside may generally use mixed colors.

sentences.zh: 祭祀之服，須合禮經，宜集通儒，更可詳議。

translations.literal: Sacrificial dress must accord with the ritual classics; learned Confucians should be assembled to discuss further in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial dress must accord with the ritual classics; learned Confucians should be assembled for further detailed discussion.

sentences.zh: 」太子庶子、攝太常少卿裴政奏曰：「竊見後周制冕，加為十二，既與前禮數乃不同，而色應五行，又非典故。

translations.literal: " The Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Acting Director of the Directorate of Ceremonials Pei Zheng memorialized: "I observe that Later Zhou regulated the mián to twelve types, which already differs from earlier ritual in number, and colors responding to the Five Phases is not according to ancient precedent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Acting Director of the Directorate of Ceremonials Pei Zheng memorialized: "I observe that Later Zhou regulated the mián to twelve types, which already differs from earlier ritual in number, and having colors respond to the Five Phases is not according to ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 謹案三代之冠，其名各別。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine that the caps of the Three Dynasties each had distinct names.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that the caps of the Three Dynasties each had distinct names.

sentences.zh: 六等之冕，承用區分，璪玉五采，隨班異飾，都無迎氣變色之文。

translations.literal: The six grades of mián continued in use with distinctions; jade pendants in five colors, ornaments differing by rank—nowhere is there text about changing colors to receive the seasonal qi.
translations.idiomatic: The six grades of mián continued in use with distinctions; jade pendants in five colors and ornaments differing by rank—nowhere is there text about changing colors to receive the seasonal qi.

sentences.zh: 唯月令者，起于秦代，乃有青旂赤玉，白駱黑衣，與四時而色變，全不言於弁冕。

translations.literal: Only the 'Monthly Ordinances,' starting from the Qin era, have green banners, red jade, white horses, and black robes, changing color with the four seasons—it says nothing at all about the biàn and mián.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Monthly Ordinances, starting from the Qin era, have green banners, red jade, white horses, and black robes, changing color with the four seasons—it says nothing at all about the biàn and mián.

sentences.zh: 五時冕色，禮既無文，稽於正典，難以經證。

translations.literal: Five-season mián colors have no text in the Rites; searching the orthodox canon, they are hard to verify by the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Five-season mián colors have no textual basis in the Rites; searching the orthodox canon, they are hard to verify by the classics.

sentences.zh: 且後魏已來，制度咸闕。

translations.literal: Moreover since Later Wei, regulations have all been deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since Later Wei, regulations have all been deficient.

sentences.zh: 天興之歲，草創繕修，所造車服，多參胡制。

translations.literal: In the year of Heavenly Inception, in initial creation and repair, the carriages and robes made mostly followed barbarian models.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of Heavenly Inception, during initial creation and repair, the carriages and robes made mostly followed barbarian models.

sentences.zh: 故魏收論之，稱為違古，是也。

translations.literal: Thus Wei Shou in his discussion called this a violation of antiquity—and he was right.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Wei Shou in his discussion called this a violation of antiquity—and he was right.

sentences.zh: 周氏因襲，將為故事，大象承統，咸取用之，輿輦衣冠，甚多迂怪。

translations.literal: The Zhou [Northern Zhou] inherited it, treating it as precedent; the Great Elephant period accepted the succession and all took and used it—the carriages, palanquins, caps, and robes were largely perverse and strange.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou inherited it, treating it as precedent; the Great Elephant period accepted the succession and all adopted it—the carriages, palanquins, caps, and robes were largely perverse and strange.

sentences.zh: 今皇隋革命，憲章前代，其魏、周輦輅不合制者，已勑有司盡令除廢，然衣冠禮器，尚且兼行。

translations.literal: Now the Sui dynasty has changed the mandate, taking the constitution and regulations from earlier dynasties; those Wei and Zhou palanquins and carriages that did not accord with regulations have already been ordered removed by the relevant offices, yet caps, robes, and ritual implements still continue in parallel use.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Sui dynasty has changed the mandate, taking its constitution and regulations from earlier dynasties; those Wei and Zhou palanquins and carriages that did not accord with regulations have already been ordered removed by the relevant offices, yet caps, robes, and ritual implements still continue in parallel use.

sentences.zh: 乃有立夏袞衣，以赤為質，迎秋平冕，用白成形，既越典章，須革其謬。

translations.literal: There are summer solstice guan robes with red as the substance, autumn equinox ping mián formed in white—since they exceed the canonical regulations, their errors must be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: There are summer solstice guan robes with red as the substance and autumn equinox ping mián formed in white—since they exceed the canonical regulations, these errors must be corrected.

sentences.zh: 謹案續漢書禮儀志云『立春之日，京都皆著青衣』，秋夏悉如其色。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine the 'Rites and Ceremonies Monograph' of the Continuation of the Book of Han, which says 'On the day of spring's commencement, the capital all wore green robes,' autumn and summer all following their respective colors.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine the Rites and Ceremonies Monograph of the Continuation of the Book of Han, which says, 'On the day of spring's commencement, the capital all wore green robes,' with autumn and summer all following their respective colors.

sentences.zh: 逮于魏、晉，迎氣五郊，行禮之人，皆同此制。

translations.literal: Reaching Wei and Jin, at the five suburban altars receiving the seasonal qi, those performing the rites all followed this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Wei and Jin, at the five suburban altars for receiving the seasonal qi, those performing the rites all followed this regulation.

sentences.zh: 考尋故事，唯幘從衣色。

translations.literal: Examining past precedents, only the zé headcloth followed the robe color.
translations.idiomatic: Examining past precedents, only the zé headcloth followed the robe color.

sentences.zh: 今請冠及冕，色並用玄，唯應著幘者，任依漢、晉。

translations.literal: Now I request that caps and mián all use black; only where the zé should be worn, let it follow Han and Jin practice.
translations.idiomatic: Now I request that caps and mián all use black; only where the zé should be worn, let it follow Han and Jin practice.

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The rescript said: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The rescript said: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 於是定令，採用東齊之法。

translations.literal: Thereupon regulations were fixed, adopting the methods of Eastern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon regulations were fixed, adopting the methods of Eastern Qi.

sentences.zh: 乘輿袞冕，垂白珠十有二旒，以組為纓，色如其綬，黈纊充耳，玉筓。

translations.literal: The imperial guan mián hung twelve white bead tassels; silk cords served as the chin strap, their color matching the sash; yellow and blue ear-plugs filled the ears; jade hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial guan mián hung twelve white bead tassels; silk cords served as the chin strap, their color matching the sash; yellow and blue ear-plugs filled the ears; jade hairpin.

sentences.zh: 玄衣，纁裳。

translations.literal: Black upper garment, vermilion lower skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Black upper garment, vermilion lower skirt.

sentences.zh: 衣，山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝五章；

translations.literal: On the upper garment: mountain, dragon, embroidered insect, fire, and ancestral vessels—five emblems;
translations.idiomatic: On the upper garment: mountain, dragon, embroidered insect, fire, and ancestral vessels—five emblems;

sentences.zh: 裳，藻、粉、米。

translations.literal: On the skirt: waterweed, grain, and rice.
translations.idiomatic: On the skirt: waterweed, grain, and rice.

sentences.zh: 黼、黻四章。

translations.literal: Fu and fe—four emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and fe—four emblems.

sentences.zh: 衣重宗彝，裳重黼黻，為十二等。

translations.literal: The upper garment emphasized ancestral vessels, the skirt emphasized fu and fe—in all, twelve grades.
translations.idiomatic: The upper garment emphasized ancestral vessels, the skirt emphasized fu and fe—in all, twelve grades.

sentences.zh: 衣褾、領織成升龍，白紗內單，黼領，青褾、襈、裾。

translations.literal: Collar and cuffs woven with ascending dragons; white gauze inner garment; fu-pattern collar; green cuffs, border, and hem.
translations.idiomatic: Collar and cuffs were woven with ascending dragons; white gauze inner garment; fu-pattern collar; green cuffs, border, and hem.

sentences.zh: 革帶，玉鈎䚢，大帶，素帶朱裏，紕其外，上以朱，下以綠。

translations.literal: Leather belt with jade hook plaque; great sash of plain silk with vermilion lining, its edges bordered, vermilion above and green below.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt with jade hook plaque; great sash of plain silk with vermilion lining, its edges bordered, vermilion above and green below.

sentences.zh: 韍隨裳色，龍、火、山三章。

translations.literal: The knee cover matched the skirt color, with dragon, fire, and mountain—three emblems.
translations.idiomatic: The knee cover matched the skirt color, with dragon, fire, and mountain—three emblems.

sentences.zh: 鹿盧玉具劍，火珠鏢首。

translations.literal: Deer-path jade-mounted sword with fire-pearl pommel.
translations.idiomatic: Deer-path jade-mounted sword with fire-pearl pommel.

sentences.zh: 白玉雙佩，玄組。

translations.literal: Paired white jade pendants on black cords.
translations.idiomatic: Paired white jade pendants on black cords.

sentences.zh: 雙大綬，六采，玄黃赤白縹綠，純玄質，長二丈四尺，五百首，廣一尺；

translations.literal: Paired great sashes in six colors—black, yellow, red, white, light blue, and green—of pure black substance, two zhang four chi in length, five hundred tassels, one chi wide;
translations.idiomatic: Paired great sashes in six colors—black, yellow, red, white, light blue, and green—of pure black substance, two zhang four chi in length, five hundred tassels, one chi wide;

sentences.zh: 小雙綬，長二尺六寸，色同大綬，而首半之，間施三玉環。

translations.literal: Paired small sashes two chi six cun in length, the same colors as the great sash but half the tassels, with three jade rings set between.
translations.idiomatic: Paired small sashes two chi six cun in length, the same colors as the great sash but half the tassels, with three jade rings set between.

sentences.zh: 朱韈，赤舄，舄加金飾。

translations.literal: Vermilion socks, red ceremonial shoes with gold ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks, red ceremonial shoes with gold ornament.

sentences.zh: 祀圓丘、方澤、感帝、明堂、五郊、雩、蜡、封禪、朝日、夕月、宗廟、社稷、籍田、廟遣上將、征還飲至、元服、納后、正月受朝及臨軒拜王公，則服之。

translations.literal: Worn when sacrificing at the Round Mound, Square Pond, Lord of the Five Emperors, Bright Hall, five suburban altars, rain prayer, la sacrifice, feng and shan rites, morning and evening moon rites, ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, plowing the sacred field, dispatching a great general from the temple, victory banquet on return from campaign, capping ceremony, empress's investiture, New Year's audience, and audience at the imperial throne to invest princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: This was worn when sacrificing at the Round Mound, Square Pond, Lord of the Five Emperors, Bright Hall, five suburban altars, rain prayer, la sacrifice, feng and shan rites, morning and evening moon rites, ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, plowing the sacred field, dispatching a great general from the temple, the victory banquet on return from campaign, the capping ceremony, empress's investiture, New Year's audience, and audience at the imperial throne to invest princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 通天冠，加金博山，附蟬，十二首，施珠翠，黑介幘，玉簪導。

translations.literal: Tongtian cap with gold Boshan ornament, attached cicada, twelve tassels, pearl and kingfisher feather ornament, black jie headcloth, jade hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Tongtian cap with gold Boshan ornament, attached cicada, twelve tassels, pearl and kingfisher feather ornament, black jie headcloth, jade hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 絳紗袍，深衣制，白紗內單，皁領、褾、襈、裾，絳紗蔽膝，白假帶，方心曲領。

translations.literal: Crimson gauze robe in deep-garment style, white gauze inner garment, black collar, cuffs, border, and hem, crimson gauze knee cover, white imitation sash, square heart and curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson gauze robe in deep-garment style, white gauze inner garment, black collar, cuffs, border, and hem, crimson gauze knee cover, white imitation sash, square heart and curved collar.

sentences.zh: 其革帶、劍、佩、綬、舄，與上同。

translations.literal: The leather belt, sword, pendants, sash, and shoes were the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: The leather belt, sword, pendants, sash, and shoes were the same as above.

sentences.zh: 若未加元服，則雙童髻，空頂黑介幘，雙玉導，加寶飾。

translations.literal: If the capping ceremony had not yet been performed, double child topknots, open-topped black jie headcloth, paired jade guides with precious ornament.
translations.idiomatic: If the capping ceremony had not yet been performed, double child topknots, open-topped black jie headcloth, paired jade guides with precious ornament.

sentences.zh: 朔日受朝、元會及冬會、諸祭還，則服之。

translations.literal: Worn for the first-day-of-month audience, New Year's assembly, winter assembly, and on return from all sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: This was worn for the first-day-of-month audience, New Year's assembly, winter assembly, and on return from all sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 武弁，金附蟬，平巾幘，餘服具服。

translations.literal: Military cap with gold attached cicada, flat zé headcloth, remaining garments as full dress.
translations.idiomatic: Military cap with gold attached cicada, flat zé headcloth, remaining garments as full dress.

sentences.zh: 講武、出征、四時蒐狩、大射、禡、類、宜社、賞祖、罰社、纂嚴，則服之。

translations.literal: Worn for martial exercises, campaigns, four-season hunts, great archery, ma and lei rites, earth-god rites, rewarding at the ancestral temple, punishing at the earth altar, and assembling the guard.
translations.idiomatic: This was worn for martial exercises, campaigns, four-season hunts, great archery, ma and lei rites, earth-god rites, rewarding at the ancestral temple, punishing at the earth altar, and assembling the guard.

sentences.zh: 黑介幘，白紗單衣，烏皮履，拜陵則服之。

translations.literal: Black jie headcloth, white gauze single garment, black leather shoes—worn when paying respects at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Black jie headcloth, white gauze single garment, black leather shoes—worn when paying respects at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 白紗帽，白練裙襦，烏皮履，視朝、聽訟及宴見賓客，皆服之。

translations.literal: White gauze cap, white silk skirt and jacket, black leather shoes—worn for holding court, hearing lawsuits, and banquets with guests.
translations.idiomatic: White gauze cap, white silk skirt and jacket, black leather shoes—worn for holding court, hearing lawsuits, and banquets with guests.

sentences.zh: 白帢，白紗單衣，烏皮履，舉哀則服之。

translations.literal: White kerchief, white gauze single garment, black leather shoes—worn when expressing mourning.
translations.idiomatic: White kerchief, white gauze single garment, black leather shoes—worn when expressing mourning.

sentences.zh: 神璽，寶而不用。

translations.literal: The Spirit Seal—precious yet not used.
translations.idiomatic: The Spirit Seal—precious yet not used.

sentences.zh: 受命璽，封禪則用之。

translations.literal: The Mandate-Receiving Seal—used for feng and shan rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Mandate-Receiving Seal—used for feng and shan rites.

sentences.zh: 「皇帝行璽」，封命諸侯及三師、三公，則用之。

translations.literal: The 'Emperor's Traveling Seal'—used when sealing commands to feudal lords and the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The "Emperor's Traveling Seal"—used when sealing commands to feudal lords and the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 「皇帝之璽」，賜諸侯及三師、三公書，則用之。

translations.literal: The 'Emperor's Seal'—used when bestowing letters on feudal lords and the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The "Emperor's Seal"—used when bestowing letters on feudal lords and the Three Preceptors and Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 「皇帝信璽」，徵諸夏兵，則用之。

translations.literal: The 'Emperor's Trust Seal'—used when mobilizing troops within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The "Emperor's Trust Seal"—used when mobilizing troops within the realm.

sentences.zh: 「天子行璽」，封命蕃國之君，則用之。

translations.literal: The 'Son of Heaven's Traveling Seal'—used when sealing commands to foreign rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The "Son of Heaven's Traveling Seal"—used when sealing commands to foreign rulers.

sentences.zh: 「天子之璽」，賜蕃國之君書，則用之。

translations.literal: The 'Son of Heaven's Seal'—used when bestowing letters on foreign rulers.
translations.idiomatic: The "Son of Heaven's Seal"—used when bestowing letters on foreign rulers.

sentences.zh: 「天子信璽」，徵蕃國兵，則用之。

translations.literal: The 'Son of Heaven's Trust Seal'—used when mobilizing foreign troops.
translations.idiomatic: The "Son of Heaven's Trust Seal"—used when mobilizing foreign troops.

sentences.zh: 常行詔勑，則用內史門下印。

translations.literal: For ordinary edicts and orders, the Inner Secretariat and Gate Department seal was used.
translations.idiomatic: For ordinary edicts and orders, the Inner Secretariat and Gate Department seal was used.

sentences.zh: 皇帝臨臣之喪，三品已上，服錫衰；

translations.literal: When the emperor attended a minister's mourning, for third rank and above, he wore tin mourning;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor attended a minister's mourning, for third rank and above he wore tin mourning;

sentences.zh: 五等諸侯，緦衰；

translations.literal: For feudal lords of the fifth rank, hemp mourning;
translations.idiomatic: for feudal lords of the fifth rank, hemp mourning;

sentences.zh: 四品已下，疑衰。

translations.literal: For fourth rank and below, doubtful mourning.
translations.idiomatic: for fourth rank and below, doubtful mourning.

sentences.zh: 皇太子袞冕，垂白珠九旒，青纊充耳，犀筓。

translations.literal: The crown prince's guan mián hung nine white bead tassels; green ear-plugs filled the ears; rhinoceros hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's guan mián hung nine white bead tassels; green ear-plugs filled the ears; rhinoceros hairpin.

sentences.zh: 玄衣，纁裳。

translations.literal: Black upper garment, vermilion lower skirt.
translations.idiomatic: Black upper garment, vermilion lower skirt.

sentences.zh: 衣，山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝五章；

translations.literal: On the upper garment: mountain, dragon, embroidered insect, fire, and ancestral vessels—five emblems;
translations.idiomatic: On the upper garment: mountain, dragon, embroidered insect, fire, and ancestral vessels—five emblems;

sentences.zh: 裳，藻、粉米、黼、黻四章。

translations.literal: On the skirt: waterweed, grain, rice, fu, and fe—four emblems.
translations.idiomatic: On the skirt: waterweed, grain, rice, fu, and fe—four emblems.

sentences.zh: 織成為之。

translations.literal: Woven to form them.
translations.idiomatic: These were woven to form them.

translations.literal: Dong Ba's monograph says: "The six mián of Han shared one form, all seven cun wide, one chi two cun long, round in front and square behind.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ba's monograph says: "The six mián of Han shared one form, all seven cun wide, one chi two cun long, round in front and square behind.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂依此為大裘冕制，青表，朱裏，不施旒纊，不通於下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they followed this as the great fur robe mián form: green exterior, vermilion lining, no tassels or ear-plugs applied, not extending below.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they followed this as the great fur robe mián form: green exterior, vermilion lining, no tassels or ear-plugs applied, not extending below.

sentences.zh: 其大裘之服，案周官注「羔裘也」。

translations.literal: The great fur robe dress: examining the commentary on the Offices of Zhou, "lamb fur robe."
translations.idiomatic: The great fur robe dress: examining the commentary on the Offices of Zhou, "lamb fur robe."

sentences.zh: 其制，準禮圖，以羔正黑者為之，取同色繒以為領袖。

translations.literal: Its form, according to the ritual illustrations, was made of properly black lamb fur, with silk of the same color for collar and sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Its form, according to the ritual illustrations, was made of properly black lamb fur, with silk of the same color for collar and sleeves.

sentences.zh: 其裳用纁，而無章飾，絳韈，赤舄。

translations.literal: Its skirt was vermilion, without patterned ornament, vermilion socks, red ceremonial shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Its skirt was vermilion, without patterned ornament, vermilion socks, red ceremonial shoes.

sentences.zh: 祀圓丘、感帝、封禪、五郊、明堂、雩、蜡，皆服之。

translations.literal: Worn when sacrificing at the Round Mound, Lord of the Five Emperors, feng and shan rites, five suburban altars, Bright Hall, rain prayer, and la sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Worn when sacrificing at the Round Mound, Lord of the Five Emperors, feng and shan rites, five suburban altars, Bright Hall, rain prayer, and la sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 袞冕之制，案禮玉藻「十有二旒」。

translations.literal: The form of guan mián: examining the "Jade Ornaments" in the Rites, "twelve tassels."
translations.idiomatic: The form of guan mián: examining the "Jade Ornaments" in the Rites, "twelve tassels."

sentences.zh: 大戴禮云：「冕而加旒，以蔽明也，琇纊塞耳，以蔽聰也。

translations.literal: The Great Dai Rites says: "Mián with tassels added to cover brightness, fine ear-plugs to stop the ears to cover hearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Dai Rites says: "Mián with tassels added to cover brightness, fine ear-plugs to stop the ears to cover hearing.

sentences.zh: 」又禮含文嘉：「前後邃延，不視邪也，加以黈纊，不聽讒也。

translations.literal: " Also the Rites' "Embodying the Auspicious Patterns": "Front and back extending far, not looking askance; adding yellow and blue ear-plugs, not listening to slander.
translations.idiomatic: " Also the Rites' "Embodying the Auspicious Patterns": "Front and back extending far, not looking askance; adding yellow and blue ear-plugs, not listening to slander.

sentences.zh: 」三王之冕，既不通制，故夫子云：「行夏之時，服周之冕。

translations.literal: " The mián of the Three Kings did not share one form, so the Master said: "Follow the Xia calendar, wear the Zhou mián.
translations.idiomatic: " The mián of the Three Kings did not share one form, so the Master said: "Follow the Xia calendar, wear the Zhou mián.

sentences.zh: 」今以采綖貫珠，為旒十二。

translations.literal: " Now colored cords strung with pearls form twelve tassels.
translations.idiomatic: " Now colored cords strung with pearls form twelve tassels.

sentences.zh: 邃延者，出冕前後而下垂之，旒齊於髆，纊齊於耳，組為纓，玉笄導。

translations.literal: Extending far means projecting before and behind the mián and hanging down; tassels level with the crown top, ear-plugs level with the ears; silk cords as chin strap, jade hairpin guide.
translations.idiomatic: Extending far means projecting before and behind the mián and hanging down; tassels level with the crown top, ear-plugs level with the ears; silk cords as chin strap, jade hairpin guide.

sentences.zh: 其為服之制，案釋名云「袞，卷也」，謂畫龍於上也。

translations.literal: The form of its dress: examining the Explaining Names, "guan, rolled up," meaning dragons painted above.
translations.idiomatic: The form of its dress: examining the Explaining Names, "guan, rolled up," meaning dragons painted above.

sentences.zh: 是時虞世基奏曰：

translations.literal: At that time Yu Shiji memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Shiji memorialized:

sentences.zh: :後周故事，升日月於旌旗，乃闕三辰，而章無十二。

translations.literal: According to Later Zhou precedent, sun and moon were raised on banners and flags, thus omitting the three luminaries, while the emblems were not twelve.
translations.idiomatic: According to Later Zhou precedent, sun and moon were raised on banners and flags, thus omitting the three luminaries, while the emblems were not twelve.

sentences.zh: 但有山、龍、華蟲作繪，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻，乃與三公不異。

translations.literal: There were only mountain, dragon, and embroidered insect as painting, ancestral vessels, waterweed, fire, grain, fu, and fe—thus no different from the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: There were only mountain, dragon, and embroidered insect as painting, ancestral vessels, waterweed, fire, grain, fu, and fe—thus no different from the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，就裏欲生分別，故衣重宗彝，裳重黼黻，合重二物，以就九章，為十二等。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang period, wishing to create distinctions within, the upper garment emphasized ancestral vessels and the skirt emphasized fu and fe, combining two repeated emblems to make nine chapters into twelve grades.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang period, wishing to create distinctions within, the upper garment emphasized ancestral vessels and the skirt emphasized fu and fe, combining two repeated emblems to make nine chapters into twelve grades.

sentences.zh: 但每一物，上下重行。

translations.literal: But each emblem was repeated above and below in rows.
translations.idiomatic: But each emblem was repeated above and below in rows.

sentences.zh: 袞服用九，鷩服用七，今重此三物，乃非典故。

translations.literal: Guan dress used nine, bi dress used seven—now repeating these three emblems is not according to ancient precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Guan dress used nine, bi dress used seven—now repeating these three emblems is not according to ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 且周氏執謙，不敢負於日月，所以綴此三象，唯施太常，天王袞衣，章乃從九。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhou practiced humility, not daring to bear sun and moon upon themselves, so they attached these three symbols only on the Grand Banner; the Heavenly King's guan robe had emblems following nine.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhou practiced humility, not daring to bear sun and moon upon themselves, so they attached these three symbols only on the Grand Banner; the Heavenly King's guan robe had emblems following nine.

sentences.zh: 但天子譬日，德在照臨，辰為帝位，月主正后，負此三物，合德齊明，自古有之，理應無惑。

translations.literal: But the Son of Heaven is like the sun, his virtue in shining forth; the stars are the emperor's position, the moon governs the principal consort—bearing these three emblems, combined virtue and equal brightness, has existed from antiquity and should not be doubted.
translations.idiomatic: But the Son of Heaven is like the sun, his virtue in shining forth; the stars are the emperor's position, the moon governs the principal consort—bearing these three emblems, combined virtue and equal brightness, has existed from antiquity and should not be doubted.

sentences.zh: 周執謙道，殊未可依，重用宗彝，又乖法服。

translations.literal: Zhou's practice of humility cannot be followed; repeating ancestral vessels again also departs from prescribed dress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's practice of humility cannot be followed; repeating ancestral vessels again also departs from prescribed dress.

sentences.zh: :今準尚書：「予欲觀古人之服，日、月、星辰、山、龍、華蟲作會，宗彝、藻、火、粉米、黼黻絺繡。

translations.literal: Now according to the Documents: "I wish to observe the dress of the ancients—sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, and embroidered insect as assembly, ancestral vessels, waterweed, fire, grain, fu and fe as fine embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Now according to the Documents: "I wish to observe the dress of the ancients—sun, moon, stars, mountain, dragon, and embroidered insect as assembly, ancestral vessels, waterweed, fire, grain, fu and fe as fine embroidery.

sentences.zh: 」具依此，於左右髆上為日月各一，當後領下而為星辰，又山、龍九物，各重行十二。

translations.literal: " Fully following this, on the left and right crown tops one sun and one moon each, stars below the back collar, and the nine emblems of mountain and dragon each repeated in twelve rows.
translations.idiomatic: " Fully following this, on the left and right crown tops one sun and one moon each, stars below the back collar, and the nine emblems of mountain and dragon each repeated in twelve rows.

sentences.zh: 又近代故實，依尚書大傳：「山龍純青，華蟲純黃，作會；

translations.literal: Also recent precedent, according to the Great Commentary on the Documents: "Mountain and dragon pure green, embroidered insect pure yellow, as assembly;
translations.idiomatic: Also recent precedent, according to the Great Commentary on the Documents: "Mountain and dragon pure green, embroidered insect pure yellow, as assembly;

sentences.zh: 宗彝純黑，藻純白，火純赤。

translations.literal: Ancestral vessels pure black, waterweed pure white, fire pure red.
translations.idiomatic: ancestral vessels pure black, waterweed pure white, fire pure red.

sentences.zh: 」以此相間，而為五采。

translations.literal: " Using these alternately, forming five colors.
translations.idiomatic: " Using these alternately, forming five colors.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄議已自非之，云：「五采相錯，非一色也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan in his deliberation already criticized this, saying: "Five colors intermixed are not one color.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan in his deliberation already criticized this, saying: "Five colors intermixed are not one color.

sentences.zh: 」今並用織成於繡，五色錯文。

translations.literal: " Now all use woven work in embroidery, five colors interwoven.
translations.idiomatic: " Now all use woven work in embroidery, five colors interwoven.

sentences.zh: 準孔安國，衣質以玄，加山、龍、華蟲、火、宗彝等，並織成為五物；

translations.literal: Following Kong Anguo, the upper garment substance black, adding mountain, dragon, embroidered insect, fire, ancestral vessels and the like, all woven as five emblems;
translations.idiomatic: Following Kong Anguo, the upper garment substance black, adding mountain, dragon, embroidered insect, fire, ancestral vessels and the like, all woven as five emblems;

sentences.zh: 裳質以纁，加藻、粉米、黼、黻之四。

translations.literal: Skirt substance vermilion, adding waterweed, grain, fu, and fe—four more.
translations.idiomatic: skirt substance vermilion, adding waterweed, grain, fu, and fe—four more.

sentences.zh: 衣裳通數，此為九章，兼上三辰，而備十二也。

translations.literal: Upper and lower garment total, this makes nine chapters, plus the three luminaries above, completing twelve.
translations.idiomatic: Upper and lower garment total, this makes nine chapters, plus the three luminaries above, completing twelve.

sentences.zh: 衣褾、領上各帖升龍，漢、晉以來，率皆如此。

translations.literal: Collar and upper border each had ascending dragons attached—since Han and Jin, all have generally been thus.
translations.idiomatic: Collar and upper border each had ascending dragons attached—since Han and Jin, all have generally been thus.

sentences.zh: 既是先王法服，不可乖於夏制，徵而用之，理將為允。

translations.literal: Since this is the sage's prescribed dress, it cannot depart from Xia models—adopting and using it is in principle acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Since this is the sage's prescribed dress, it cannot depart from Xia models—adopting and using it is in principle acceptable.

sentences.zh: 墨勑曰：「可。

translations.literal: Imperial rescript: "Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial rescript: "Approved.

sentences.zh: 」承以單衣。

translations.literal: " Under it a single garment.
translations.idiomatic: " Under it a single garment.

sentences.zh: 又案董巴輿服志宗廟冕服云：「絳領、袖為內單衣。

translations.literal: Also examining Dong Ba's Carriages and Robes Monograph on ancestral temple mián dress: "Crimson collar and sleeves as inner single garment.
translations.idiomatic: Also examining Dong Ba's Carriages and Robes Monograph on ancestral temple mián dress: "Crimson collar and sleeves as inner single garment.

sentences.zh: 」又車服雜記曰：「天子釋奠、郊祭而單衣，以絳緣。

translations.literal: " Also the Miscellaneous Notes on Carriages and Robes say: "The Son of Heaven at libation sacrifice and suburban sacrifice wore single garment with crimson border.
translations.idiomatic: " Also the Miscellaneous Notes on Carriages and Robes say: "The Son of Heaven at libation sacrifice and suburban sacrifice wore single garment with crimson border.

sentences.zh: 」今用白紗為內單，黼領，絳褾，青裾及襈。

translations.literal: " Now white gauze serves as inner single garment, fu-pattern collar, crimson border, green hem and cuff border.
translations.idiomatic: " Now white gauze serves as inner single garment, fu-pattern collar, crimson border, green hem and cuff border.

sentences.zh: 革帶，玉鉤䚢，大帶朱裏，紕其外。

translations.literal: Leather belt, jade hook plaque, great sash with vermilion lining, its edges bordered.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt, jade hook plaque, great sash with vermilion lining, its edges bordered.

sentences.zh: 紐約用組，上加朱𩊊。

translations.literal: The buckle cord used silk cords, with vermilion knee cover added above.
translations.idiomatic: The buckle cord used silk cords, with vermilion knee cover added above.

sentences.zh: 又案說文：「韠，韍也。

translations.literal: Also examining the Explaining Writing: "Bi, knee cover.
translations.idiomatic: Also examining the Explaining Writing: "Bi, knee cover.

sentences.zh: 所以蔽前。

translations.literal: That by which the front is covered.
translations.idiomatic: That by which the front is covered.

sentences.zh: 」禮記曰：「有虞氏韍，夏后氏山，殷火，周龍章。

translations.literal: " The Record of Rites says: "The Youyu clan's knee cover, Xia's mountain, Shang's fire, Zhou's dragon emblem.
translations.idiomatic: " The Record of Rites says: "The Youyu clan's knee cover, Xia's mountain, Shang's fire, Zhou's dragon emblem.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄曰：「冕之韍也，舜始作之，以尊祭服。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan says: "The mián's knee cover—Shun first made it to honor sacrificial dress.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Xuan says: "The mián's knee cover—Shun first made it to honor sacrificial dress.

sentences.zh: 禹、湯至周，增以文飾。

translations.literal: From Yu and Tang to Zhou, patterned ornament was added.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu and Tang to Zhou, patterned ornament was added.

sentences.zh: 」禮記曰：「君朱韠。

translations.literal: " The Record of Rites says: "The ruler's vermilion knee cover.
translations.idiomatic: " The Record of Rites says: "The ruler's vermilion knee cover.

sentences.zh: 」鄭曰：「韠象裳色。

translations.literal: " Zheng says: "The knee cover represents the skirt color.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng says: "The knee cover represents the skirt color.

sentences.zh: 」今依白武通注，以蔽裳前，上闊一尺，象天數也；

translations.literal: " Now following the White Tiger Pass commentary, to cover before the skirt, one chi wide above, representing heaven's number;
translations.idiomatic: " Now following the White Tiger Pass commentary, to cover before the skirt, one chi wide above, representing heaven's number;

sentences.zh: 下闊二尺，象地數也；

translations.literal: Two chi wide below, representing earth's number;
translations.idiomatic: two chi wide below, representing earth's number;

sentences.zh: 長三尺，象三才也；

translations.literal: Three chi long, representing the three powers;
translations.idiomatic: three chi long, representing the three powers;

sentences.zh: 加龍章山火，以備三代之法也。

translations.literal: Adding dragon emblem, mountain, and fire to complete the law of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: adding dragon emblem, mountain, and fire to complete the law of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 於是制袞冕之服，玄衣，纁裳，合九章為十二等。

translations.literal: Thereupon guan mián dress was made: black upper garment, vermilion lower skirt, nine chapters combined into twelve grades.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon guan mián dress was made: black upper garment, vermilion lower skirt, nine chapters combined into twelve grades.

sentences.zh: 白紗內單，黼領，青褾、襈。

translations.literal: White gauze inner garment, fu-pattern collar, green border and cuff border.
translations.idiomatic: White gauze inner garment, fu-pattern collar, green border and cuff border.

sentences.zh: 革帶，玉鉤䚢，大帶，韍，鹿盧玉具劍，火珠鏢首，白玉雙佩，玄組，大、小綬。

translations.literal: Leather belt, jade hook plaque, great sash, knee cover, deer-path jade-mounted sword with fire-pearl pommel, paired white jade pendants on black cords, great and small sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Leather belt, jade hook plaque, great sash, knee cover, deer-path jade-mounted sword with fire-pearl pommel, paired white jade pendants on black cords, great and small sashes.

sentences.zh: 朱韈，赤舄，舄飾以金。

translations.literal: Vermilion socks, red ceremonial shoes, shoes ornamented with gold.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion socks, red ceremonial shoes, shoes ornamented with gold.

sentences.zh: 宗廟、社稷、籍田、方澤、朝日、夕月、遣將授律、征還飲至、加元服、納后、正冬受朝、臨軒拜爵，皆服之。

translations.literal: Worn for ancestral temple, altars of soil and grain, plowing the sacred field, Square Pond, morning and evening moon rites, dispatching generals with military codes, victory banquet on return from campaign, capping ceremony, empress's investiture, midwinter audience, and audience at the imperial throne to invest nobility.

translations.literal: The form of the tongtian cap: examining Dong Ba's monograph: "Cap nine cun high, form upright, top slightly slanting back, then straight down as iron rolled beam, High Mountain in front.
translations.idiomatic: The form of the tongtian cap: examining Dong Ba's monograph: "Cap nine cun high, form upright, top slightly slanting back, then straight down as iron rolled beam, High Mountain in front.

sentences.zh: 」故禮圖或謂之高山冠也。

translations.literal: " Thus the ritual illustrations sometimes call it the High Mountain cap.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the ritual illustrations sometimes call it the High Mountain cap.

sentences.zh: 晉起居注，成帝咸和五年，制詔殿內曰：「平天、通天冠，並不能佳，可更修理之。

translations.literal: The Jin Daily Records, in the fifth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng, edict in the palace hall: "The flat heaven and tongtian caps are both not good; they should be repaired further.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Daily Records, in the fifth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng, edict in the palace hall: "The flat heaven and tongtian caps are both not good; they should be repaired further.

sentences.zh: 」雖在禮無文，故知天子所冠，其來久矣。

translations.literal: " Though without text in the Rites, one knows the Son of Heaven's cap has existed long.
translations.idiomatic: " Though without text in the Rites, one knows the Son of Heaven's cap has existed long.

sentences.zh: 又徐氏輿服注曰：「通天冠，高九寸，黑介幘，金博山。

translations.literal: Also Master Xu's Carriages and Robes commentary says: "Tongtian cap, nine cun high, black jie headcloth, gold Boshan.
translations.idiomatic: Also Master Xu's Carriages and Robes commentary says: "Tongtian cap, nine cun high, black jie headcloth, gold Boshan.

sentences.zh: 」徐爰亦曰：「博山附蟬，謂之金顏。

translations.literal: " Xu Ai also says: "Boshan with attached cicada is called gold countenance.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Ai also says: "Boshan with attached cicada is called gold countenance.

sentences.zh: 」今制依此，不通於下，獨天子元會臨軒服之。

translations.literal: " The present form follows this, not extending below; only the Son of Heaven wears it at New Year's assembly and audience at the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: " The present form follows this, not extending below; only the Son of Heaven wears it at New Year's assembly and audience at the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 其服絳紗袍，深衣制，白紗內單，皁領、褾、裾、襈，絳紗蔽膝，白假帶，方心曲領。

translations.literal: Its dress: crimson gauze robe in deep-garment style, white gauze inner garment, black collar, border, hem, and cuff border, crimson gauze knee cover, white imitation sash, square heart and curved collar.
translations.idiomatic: Its dress: crimson gauze robe in deep-garment style, white gauze inner garment, black collar, border, hem, and cuff border, crimson gauze knee cover, white imitation sash, square heart and curved collar.

sentences.zh: 其劍、佩、綬、舄、革帶，皆與上同。

translations.literal: The sword, pendants, sash, shoes, and leather belt were all the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: The sword, pendants, sash, shoes, and leather belt were all the same as above.

sentences.zh: 元冬饗會、諸祭還，則服之。

translations.literal: Worn at midwinter feast assembly and on return from all sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Worn at midwinter feast assembly and on return from all sacrifices.

translations.idiomatic: At the four seasons' inspection of the new moon, the inner garment, collar, and cuff border each followed the color of its direction.

sentences.zh: 唯秋方色白，以綠代之。

translations.literal: Only for autumn the directional color was white, replaced with green.
translations.idiomatic: Only for autumn the directional color was white, replaced with green.

translations.idiomatic: The form of the far-wandering cap: examining Han Miscellaneous Affairs: "The crown prince and all princes wore it.

sentences.zh: 」故淮南子曰：「楚莊王冠通梁，組纓。

translations.literal: " Thus the Huainanzi says: "King Zhuang of Chu wore the cap with connecting beam, silk cord tassel.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus the Huainanzi says: "King Zhuang of Chu wore the cap with connecting beam, silk cord tassel.

sentences.zh: 」注云：「通梁，遠遊也。

translations.literal: " The commentary says: "Connecting beam is far-wandering.
translations.idiomatic: " The commentary says: "Connecting beam is far-wandering.

sentences.zh: 」晉令：「皇太子諸王，給遠遊冠。

translations.literal: " Jin regulations: "Crown prince and all princes were given far-wandering caps.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin regulations: "Crown prince and all princes were given far-wandering caps.

sentences.zh: 」徐氏雜注曰：「天子雜服，遠遊五梁。

translations.literal: " Master Xu's miscellaneous commentary says: "The Son of Heaven's miscellaneous dress, far-wandering five beams.
translations.idiomatic: " Master Xu's miscellaneous commentary says: "The Son of Heaven's miscellaneous dress, far-wandering five beams.

sentences.zh: 太子諸王三梁。

translations.literal: Crown prince and princes three beams.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince and princes three beams.
